title: A Right to Appeal
briefing: A resource-allocation model has issued ration limits that keep total demand within supply. Appeals reveal households whose medical and care needs are missing from the records. AI recommendation: Keep current quotas and review disputes after the demand peak. This prioritizes service resilience under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The meters can apply exceptions quickly, but many concurrent changes make demand forecasts less dependable.
private_intelligence.community: A public appeal route would improve legitimacy only if people without documents can obtain an independent assessment.
private_intelligence.economy: Blanket increases for disputed accounts would exceed procurement reserves; targeted advances have a smaller but real cost.
private_intelligence.safety: Some medical uses cannot safely wait for next-day review, yet a vague emergency category invites inconsistent decisions.

choices.title: Enforce Limits Before Review
choices.description: Keep current quotas and review disputes after the demand peak.
choices.consequence: Supply remains predictable and operating costs stay controlled, but deferred medical exceptions reduce safety and trust.

choices.title: Open an Independent Appeal Desk
choices.description: Fund rapid reviewed exceptions for medical and care needs.
choices.consequence: Urgent needs receive a credible route and households cooperate, while forecast uncertainty and review costs increase.

choices.title: Raise Limits for All Disputed Cases
choices.description: Grant temporary extra supply wherever an appeal is filed.
choices.consequence: Rapid access rebuilds goodwill and supports local activity, but poorly bounded demand and uneven urgency threaten service and safety.
